Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

Eight steps (guide)

Describe → Inventory → Forms → Origin → Context → Meaning → Critical → Circulation.

Step 7 (critical) is mandatory. A clean diary without power questions fails.

Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

1 · Describe the process first

Say what happened — task, sequence, tools — before you praise the result.

Image: A 1921 Gilbreth process chart of the 'present method' for ordering printed forms: numbered circles and squares run down the page, each labelled with who does what.

Process Chart for Ordering Blank Forms – Present Method, 1921 · Frank B. Gilbreth and Lillian M. Gilbreth · Rights under review · Source

Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

2 · Language ≠ medium ≠ support

Where does the technique act: code, channel/genre, or material/file? Three questions.

Example: constraint cards (language) in a workshop (medium) on paper or an app (support).

Image: A wooden Jacquard loom in a museum: warp threads stretched on one side and a long chain of punched cards hanging on the other, the cards carrying the woven pattern.

A Jacquard loom showing information punchcards · Stephen C. Dickson · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Source

Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

3 · Open, then close

A process often needs both: invent many options, then select what fits the brief.

The same creative act may involve both divergent and convergent thinking.

(Craft 2000, 30)

Course diagram · Koch triangle · #5cc4358a9bdb · Original course SVG

Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

4 · Divergent is a hallmark — not the whole job

Opening many paths matters; so does closing under constraints.

Divergent thinking has been widely regarded as a major hallmark of creativity.

(Chen 2011, 25)

Image: An early-19th-century design sheet with six chairs in two rows, each a different frame and back, all sharing the same scarlet upholstery.

Design for Six Chairs with Scarlet Upholstery · Anonymous designer (early 19th century); The Metropolitan Museum of Art (CC0) · CC0 1.0 · Source

Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

5 · Process is also material

Composition is not only steps on paper — media and materials shape how ideas get realised.

As a compositional device and an agent for realising ideas in performance, it, too, has become a material medium in many of our examples.

(Eckersall, Grehan, and Scheer 2017, 211)

Convergent/divergent still matters (lesson text); here ask what the medium does to the process.

Image: A 19th-century wood engraving of Loïe Fuller's Serpentine Dance in eight panels: the dancer's swirling silk takes the shape of serpents, a basket, a propeller and butterflies.

La danse serpentine, Loïe Fuller et ses transformations · Unknown author (before 1900) · Public domain · Source

Master Lecture · Creative process analysis

6 · Critical: a score is not the designer

A fluency score on a toy task does not prove judgement inside a real brief.

the ability of divergent thinking with a paper clip may tell us little about an individual's talent in music.

(Chen 2011, 26)

Also ask: whose labour is visible? Does GenAI hide authorship? (C1–C3 hooks)
